83: func isPreCodeContextStages(stages []StageState) bool {

88: 	for i := range legacy {
89: 		if stages[i].Stage != legacy[i] {
90: 			return false
91: 		}
92: 	}
93: 	return true
94: }

96: func interpretPreCodeContextStages(sp Sprint, stages []StageState) []StageState {
97: 	out := make([]StageState, 0, len(stages)+1)
98: 	out = append(out, stages[0])
99: 	inserted := StageState{Stage: StageCodeContext, Status: StatusMissing, Path: ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageCodeContext)}
100: 	if stages[0].Status == StatusComplete {
101: 		inserted.Status = StatusReady
102: 		for _, later := range stages[1:] {
103: 			if later.Status != StatusMissing {
104: 				inserted.Status = StatusSkipped
105: 				inserted.LastRunAt = stages[0].LastRunAt
106: 				break
107: 			}
108: 		}
109: 	}
110: 	out = append(out, inserted)
111: 	out = append(out, stages[1:]...)
112: 	return out
113: }

128: // legacyFlowState reports the original versioned map-based planning state.
129: // It predates durable review/smoke attempt ownership, so recovery has no live
130: // attempt to reconcile and must preserve the file for compatibility.
131: func legacyFlowState(root string, s Sprint) bool {
132: 	path, err := FlowStatePath(root, s)
133: 	if err != nil {

143: 	}

145: 		return false
146: 	}
147: 	return header.SchemaVersion == 0 && header.Version == 1
148: }

150: func migrateFlowStateV1(root string, sp Sprint, state FlowState) FlowState {
151: 	state.SchemaVersion = FlowStateSchemaVersion
152: 	if isPreCodeContextStages(state.Stages) {
153: 		state.Stages = interpretPreCodeContextStages(sp, state.Stages)
154: 	}
155: 	if state.Review != nil {
156: 		r := state.Review
157: 		r.Stale = true
158: 		if r.Status == ReviewCompleted {

160: 			if digest == "" {
161: 				digest = "legacy-unverifiable"
162: 			}
163: 			if r.Fingerprint == "" {
164: 				r.Fingerprint = "legacy-unverifiable"
165: 			}

167: 			if completedAt.IsZero() {
168: 				completedAt = state.UpdatedAt
169: 			}
170: 			r.ArtifactDigest = digest
171: 			r.LastComplete = &ReviewCompletion{Verdict: r.Verdict, Artifact: r.Path, ArtifactDigest: digest, InputFingerprint: r.Fingerprint, CompletedAt: completedAt}
172: 		}

179: 			if digest == "" {

194: func derefTime(value *time.Time) time.Time {

196: 		return time.Time{}

201: func SaveFlowState(root string, s Sprint, state FlowState) error {
202: 	// Planning-stage refreshes must not erase the last complete verification
203: 	// evidence. Explicit stage writers load and replace their own record.
204: 	if state.Review == nil || state.Smoke == nil || state.QA == nil {
205: 		if prior, err := LoadFlowState(root, s); err == nil {
206: 			if state.Review == nil {
207: 				state.Review = prior.Review
208: 			}
209: 			if state.Smoke == nil {
210: 				state.Smoke = prior.Smoke
211: 			}
212: 			if state.QA == nil {
213: 				state.QA = prior.QA
214: 			}
215: 		} else if !errors.Is(err, ErrFlowStateMissing) {
216: 			return err
217: 		}
218: 	}
219: 	if authoritative, err := FlowStateInDatabase(root, s); err != nil {
220: 		return err
221: 	} else if authoritative {
222: 		if err := saveFlowStateDatabase(root, s, state); err != nil {
223: 			return err
224: 		}
225: 		if !flowStateCheckpoint(state) {
226: 			return nil
227: 		}
228: 		return saveFlowStateWithHooks(root, s, state, atomicWriteHooks{})
229: 	}
230: 	return saveFlowStateWithHooks(root, s, state, atomicWriteHooks{})
231: }

233: func flowStateCheckpoint(state FlowState) bool {
234: 	for _, stage := range state.Stages {
235: 		if stage.Status != StatusComplete && stage.Status != StatusFailed && stage.Status != StatusSkipped {
236: 			return false
237: 		}
238: 	}
239: 	return len(state.Stages) > 0
240: }

242: func saveFlowStateWithHooks(root string, s Sprint, state FlowState, hooks atomicWriteHooks) error {
243: 	path, err := FlowStatePath(root, s)
244: 	if err != nil {
245: 		return err
246: 	}
247: 	state.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()
248: 	if err := ValidateFlowState(root, s, state, path); err != nil {
249: 		return err
250: 	}
251: 	content, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
252: 	if err != nil {
253: 		return fmt.Errorf("marshal flow state %s: %w", path, err)
254: 	}
255: 	content = append(content, '\n')
256: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
257: 		return fmt.Errorf("create flow state directory %s: %w", filepath.Dir(path), err)
258: 	}
259: 	temp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".flow-state.*.tmp")
260: 	if err != nil {
261: 		return fmt.Errorf("create temporary flow state %s: %w", path, err)
262: 	}
263: 	tempPath := temp.Name()
264: 	cleanup := true
265: 	defer func() {
266: 		if cleanup {
267: 			_ = os.Remove(tempPath)
268: 		}
269: 	}()
270: 	if _, err := temp.Write(content); err != nil {
271: 		_ = temp.Close()
272: 		return fmt.Errorf("write temporary flow state %s: %w", tempPath, err)
273: 	}
274: 	if err := temp.Sync(); err != nil {
275: 		_ = temp.Close()
276: 		return fmt.Errorf("flush temporary flow state %s: %w", tempPath, err)
277: 	}
278: 	if err := temp.Close(); err != nil {
279: 		return fmt.Errorf("close temporary flow state %s: %w", tempPath, err)
280: 	}
281: 	if hooks.BeforeRename != nil {
282: 		if err := hooks.BeforeRename(path); err != nil {
283: 			return fmt.Errorf("prepare flow state rename %s: %w", path, err)
284: 		}
285: 	}
286: 	if err := os.Rename(tempPath, path); err != nil {
287: 		return fmt.Errorf("rename flow state %s: %w", path, err)
288: 	}
289: 	cleanup = false
290: 	syncDir(filepath.Dir(path))
291: 	return nil
292: }

294: func ValidateFlowState(root string, s Sprint, state FlowState, path string) error {
295: 	if state.SchemaVersion == 0 {
296: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing schemaVersion", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
297: 	}
298: 	if state.SchemaVersion != FlowStateSchemaVersion {
299: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: schemaVersion %d", ErrFlowStateUnsupported, path, state.SchemaVersion)
300: 	}
301: 	if state.Project == "" || state.Sprint == "" || state.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
302: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing required top-level fields", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
303: 	}
304: 	if state.Project != s.Project {
305: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: project mismatch %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Project)
306: 	}
307: 	if state.Sprint != s.Slug {
308: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: sprint mismatch %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Sprint)
309: 	}
310: 	if len(state.Stages) != len(PlanningStages()) {
311: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: expected %d stages", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, len(PlanningStages()))
312: 	}
313: 	seen := map[PlanningStage]bool{}
314: 	for i, stage := range state.Stages {
315: 		if stage.Stage != PlanningStages()[i] {
316: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %d is %q; expected %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, i, stage.Stage, PlanningStages()[i])
317: 		}
318: 		if !ValidStage(stage.Stage) {
319: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsupported stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
320: 		}
321: 		if seen[stage.Stage] {
322: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: duplicate stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
323: 		}
324: 		seen[stage.Stage] = true
325: 		if !ValidStatus(stage.Status) {
326: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsupported status %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, stage.Status)
327: 		}
328: 		if stage.Path == "" {
329: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %d missing path", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, i)
330: 		}
331: 		if filepath.IsAbs(stage.Path) || strings.HasPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(stage.Path))), "../") {
332: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe path", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
333: 		}
334: 		if _, err := resolveSprintContained(root, s, stage.Path); err != nil {
335: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe path: %w", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, err)
336: 		}
337: 		if strings.ContainsAny(stage.Error, "\x00\r\n") {
338: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe error detail", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
339: 		}
340: 		switch stage.LatestOutcome {
341: 		case "", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted", "cleanup_uncertain":
342: 		default:
343: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsupported latest outcome %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, stage.LatestOutcome)
344: 		}
345: 	}
346: 	for _, expected := range PlanningStages() {
347: 		if !seen[expected] {
348: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, expected)
349: 		}
350: 	}
351: 	if state.Review != nil {
352: 		if err := validateReviewStageState(root, s, *state.Review, path); err != nil {
353: 			return err
354: 		}
355: 	}
356: 	if state.Smoke != nil {
357: 		if err := validateSmokeStageState(root, s, *state.Smoke, path); err != nil {
358: 			return err
359: 		}
360: 	}
361: 	if state.QA != nil {
362: 		if err := validateQAFlowSummary(root, s, *state.QA, path); err != nil {
363: 			return err
364: 		}
365: 	}
366: 	return nil
367: }
368:

192: // withStageOverrides returns a service copy whose stage runtime map is merged
193: // with request-scoped stage model/variant overrides. Configured defaults stay
194: // unchanged for stages without an entry.
195: func (s Service) withStageOverrides(overrides map[PlanningStage]StageRuntime) Service {
196: 	if len(overrides) == 0 {
197: 		return s
198: 	}
199: 	merged := make(map[PlanningStage]StageRuntime, len(s.stageRuntime)+len(overrides))
200: 	for stage, override := range s.stageRuntime {
201: 		merged[stage] = override
202: 	}
203: 	for stage, override := range overrides {
204: 		if override.Model == "" && override.Variant == "" {
205: 			continue
206: 		}
207: 		current := merged[stage]
208: 		if override.Model != "" {
209: 			current.Model = override.Model
210: 		}
211: 		if override.Variant != "" {
212: 			current.Variant = override.Variant
213: 		}
214: 		merged[stage] = current
215: 	}
216: 	s.stageRuntime = merged
217: 	return s
218: }

229: func (s Service) Status(projectRef, sprintRef string) (StatusSummary, error) {
230: 	projects, err := project.DiscoverProjects(s.root)
231: 	if err != nil {
232: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
233: 	}
234: 	p, err := project.ResolveProject(projects, projectRef)
235: 	if err != nil {
236: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
237: 	}
238: 	sprints, err := DiscoverSprints(s.root, p)
239: 	if err != nil {
240: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
241: 	}
242: 	sp, err := ResolveSprint(sprints, sprintRef)
243: 	if err != nil {
244: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
245: 	}
246: 	if !inside(p.Path, sp.Path) {
247: 		return StatusSummary{}, fmt.Errorf("sprint path mismatch for %q", sp.Slug)
248: 	}
249: 	legacyCodeContextState := preCodeContextFlowState(s.root, sp)
250: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, sp)
251: 	stateLoaded := err == nil
252: 	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrFlowStateMissing) {
253: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
254: 	}
255: 	snap, err := s.store.ReadArtifacts(sp)
256: 	if err != nil {
257: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
258: 	}
259: 	var prior []StageState
260: 	if stateLoaded {
261: 		prior = state.Stages
262: 	}
263: 	stages := DeriveStages(sp, snap, prior)
264: 	refreshed := NewFlowState(sp, stages, s.now())
265: 	if stateLoaded {
266: 		refreshed.Review = state.Review
267: 		refreshed.Smoke = state.Smoke
268: 		refreshed.QA = state.QA
269: 		if refreshed.Review != nil && refreshed.Review.Fingerprint != "" {
270: 			manifest, reviewFindings, reviewErr := s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, ReviewRequest{})
271: 			refreshed.Review.Stale = reviewErr != nil || len(reviewFindings) > 0 || (strictCompletedReviewSnapshotFreshness && manifest.Fingerprint != refreshed.Review.Fingerprint)
272: 			if !refreshed.Review.Stale {
273: 				content, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageReview)
274: 				validationManifest := manifest
275: 				if !strictCompletedReviewSnapshotFreshness {
276: 					validationManifest.Fingerprint = refreshed.Review.Fingerprint
277: 				}
278: 				refreshed.Review.Stale = readErr != nil || len(ValidateReviewContent(content, validationManifest)) > 0 || refreshed.Review.ArtifactDigest == "" || hashBytes([]byte(content)) != refreshed.Review.ArtifactDigest
279: 			}
280: 		}
281: 		if refreshed.Smoke != nil {
282: 			smokePath, pathErr := ArtifactPath(s.root, sp, StageSmoke)
283: 			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(smokePath)
284: 			invalid := pathErr != nil || readErr != nil || len(ValidateSmokeContent(string(data))) > 0
285: 			fingerprintMismatch := readErr == nil && refreshed.Smoke.SmokeFingerprint != "" && refreshed.Smoke.SmokeFingerprint != hashBytes(data)
286: 			reviewMismatch := refreshed.Review == nil || refreshed.Review.Stale || refreshed.Smoke.ReviewFingerprint != refreshed.Review.Fingerprint
287: 			refreshed.Smoke.Stale = invalid || fingerprintMismatch || reviewMismatch
288: 			refreshed.Smoke.Reconciliation = fingerprintMismatch || (readErr == nil && refreshed.Smoke.SmokeFingerprint == "")
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: 	if s.statusWrites && !legacyCodeContextState {
292: 		if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, refreshed); err != nil {
293: 			return StatusSummary{}, err
294: 		}
295: 	}
296: 	flowPath, err := FlowStatePath(s.root, sp)
297: 	if err != nil {
298: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
299: 	}
300: 	var executeState *ExecuteRunState
301: 	var historicalExecutionStatus string
302: 	loadedExecute, executeErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
303: 	if executeErr != nil && !errors.Is(executeErr, ErrExecuteRunStateMissing) {
304: 		if legacyStatus, ok := LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus(s.root, sp); ok {
305: 			historicalExecutionStatus = legacyStatus
306: 		} else {
307: 			return StatusSummary{}, executeErr
308: 		}
309: 	}
310: 	if executeErr == nil {
311: 		executeState = &loadedExecute
312: 	}
313: 	runStatePath, err := ExecuteRunStatePath(s.root, sp)
314: 	if err != nil {
315: 		return StatusSummary{}, err
316: 	}
317: 	verification := VerificationStatus{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug}
318: 	if historicalExecutionStatus == "" {
319: 		var verificationErr error
320: 		verification, verificationErr = s.VerificationStatus(projectRef, sprintRef)
321: 		if verificationErr != nil && !errors.Is(verificationErr, ErrFlowStateMissing) {
322: 			return StatusSummary{}, verificationErr
323: 		}
324: 	} else {
325: 		verification.Assessment = AssessmentNotApplicable
326: 		verification.NextAction = "Historical terminal execution evidence is preserved; modern review and smoke evidence is not available."
327: 	}
328: 	return StatusSummary{
329: 		Project:                   sp.Project,
330: 		Sprint:                    sp.Slug,
331: 		SprintRoot:                workspace.Rel(s.root, sp.Path),
332: 		FlowStatePath:             workspace.Rel(s.root, flowPath),
333: 		Stages:                    stages,
334: 		ExecuteState:              executeState,
335: 		HistoricalExecutionStatus: historicalExecutionStatus,
336: 		ExecutePath:               ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute),
337: 		RunStatePath:              workspace.Rel(s.root, runStatePath),
338: 		Review:                    refreshed.Review,
339: 		ReviewPath:                ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageReview),
340: 		Smoke:                     refreshed.Smoke,
341: 		SmokePath:                 ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageSmoke),
342: 		QA:                        refreshed.QA,
343: 		Verification:              verification,
344: 	}, nil
345: }

583: func (s Service) FlowRequirements(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req FlowRequest) (FlowResult, error) {
584: 	if err := validateFlowTarget(req.To); err != nil {
585: 		return FlowResult{}, err
586: 	}
587: 	sp, catalog, docs, err := s.resolveSprintForRequirements(projectRef, sprintRef, !req.DryRun)
588: 	if err != nil {
589: 		return FlowResult{}, err
590: 	}
591: 	now := s.now().UTC()
592: 	prompt := RenderRequirementsPrompt(s.root, sp, catalog, docs)
593: 	if req.DryRun {
594: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, DryRun: true, Message: prompt.Prompt}, nil
595: 	}
596: 	if s.runtime == nil {
597: 		err := fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for requirements flow")
598: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
599: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
600: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Stages: stages}, err
601: 	}
602: 	runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(prompt.Prompt, map[string]string{"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageRequirements)})
603: 	runtimeReq.Validation = s.requirementsValidationSpec(sp)
604: 	runtimeResult, err := s.startPlanningStageRun(ctx, sp, StageRequirements, runtimeReq)
605: 	if err != nil {
606: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
607: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
608: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
609: 	}
610: 	content, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageRequirements)
611: 	if err != nil {
612: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
613: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
614: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
615: 	}
616: 	findings := ValidateRequirementsContent(content)
617: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
618: 		runtimeResult, findings, err = s.repairGeneratedArtifact(ctx, runtimeReq, runtimeResult, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageRequirements), findings, func() []ValidationFinding {
619: 			data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageRequirements)
620: 			if readErr != nil {
621: 				return []ValidationFinding{finding("requirements.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageRequirements), "missing requirements", readErr.Error(), "Generate requirements.md.")}
622: 			}
623: 			return ValidateRequirementsContent(data)
624: 		})
625: 		if err != nil {
626: 			stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
627: 			_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
628: 			return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
629: 		}
630: 	}
631: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
632: 		err := fmt.Errorf("generated requirements.md failed validation")
633: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
634: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
635: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages, Findings: findings}, err
636: 	}
637: 	stages := flowRequirementsSuccessStages(sp, now)
638: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now)); err != nil {
639: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
640: 	}
641: 	_ = s.cleanupPlanningStageSessions(ctx, sp, StageRequirements, runtimeResult)
642: 	return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages, Message: "requirements complete"}, nil
643: }

907: 	}
908: 	if req.To != StageAreaReasoning && req.To != StageReasoning {
909: 		return FlowResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported reasoning flow target %q", req.To)
910: 	}
911: 	sp, inputs, catalog, err := s.resolveSprintInputsForFlow(projectRef, sprintRef, !req.DryRun)
912: 	if err != nil {
913: 		return FlowResult{}, err
914: 	}
915: 	now := s.now().UTC()

917: 		err := fmt.Errorf("requirements.md is empty or contains placeholder content")

919: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
920: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, DryRun: req.DryRun, Stages: stages}, err
921: 	}
922: 	handbookManifest, handbookFindings := BuildHandbookManifest(s.root, sp, inputs, catalog)

924: 		data, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageTechnicalHandbook)

927: 		} else {

929: 		}
930: 	}

932: 	findings = append(findings, handbookFindings...)
933: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
934: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
935: 		err := fmt.Errorf("reasoning prerequisites failed validation")
936: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)

956: func (s Service) resolveSprintInputsWithCreate(projectRef, sprintRef string, createMissing bool) (Sprint, PlanningInputs, project.ProjectIndex, error) {
957: 	projects, err := project.DiscoverProjects(s.root)
958: 	if err != nil {
959: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
960: 	}
961: 	p, err := project.ResolveProject(projects, projectRef)
962: 	if err != nil {
963: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
964: 	}
965: 	sprints, err := DiscoverSprints(s.root, p)
966: 	if err != nil {
967: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
968: 	}
969: 	sp, err := ResolveSprint(sprints, sprintRef)
970: 	if err != nil {
971: 		var refErr RefError
972: 		if !createMissing || !errors.As(err, &refErr) || refErr.Ambiguous {
973: 			return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
974: 		}
975: 		sp, err = s.createSprintSkeleton(p, sprintRef)
976: 		if err != nil {
977: 			return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
978: 		}
979: 	}
980: 	if !inside(p.Path, sp.Path) {
981: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, fmt.Errorf("sprint path mismatch for %q", sp.Slug)
982: 	}
983: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
984: 	if err != nil {
985: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, err
986: 	}
987: 	catalog, parseFindings := project.ParseProjectIndex(inputs.ProjectIndex)
988: 	if len(parseFindings) > 0 {
989: 		return Sprint{}, PlanningInputs{}, project.ProjectIndex{}, fmt.Errorf("project-index.md has malformed catalog rows")
990: 	}
991: 	return sp, inputs, catalog, nil
992: }

583: func (s Service) FlowRequirements(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req FlowRequest) (FlowResult, error) {
584: 	if err := validateFlowTarget(req.To); err != nil {
585: 		return FlowResult{}, err
586: 	}
587: 	sp, catalog, docs, err := s.resolveSprintForRequirements(projectRef, sprintRef, !req.DryRun)
588: 	if err != nil {
589: 		return FlowResult{}, err
590: 	}
591: 	now := s.now().UTC()
592: 	prompt := RenderRequirementsPrompt(s.root, sp, catalog, docs)
593: 	if req.DryRun {
594: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, DryRun: true, Message: prompt.Prompt}, nil
595: 	}
596: 	if s.runtime == nil {
597: 		err := fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for requirements flow")
598: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
599: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
600: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Stages: stages}, err
601: 	}
602: 	runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(prompt.Prompt, map[string]string{"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageRequirements)})
603: 	runtimeReq.Validation = s.requirementsValidationSpec(sp)
604: 	runtimeResult, err := s.startPlanningStageRun(ctx, sp, StageRequirements, runtimeReq)
605: 	if err != nil {
606: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
607: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
608: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
609: 	}
610: 	content, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageRequirements)
611: 	if err != nil {
612: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
613: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
614: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
615: 	}
616: 	findings := ValidateRequirementsContent(content)
617: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
618: 		runtimeResult, findings, err = s.repairGeneratedArtifact(ctx, runtimeReq, runtimeResult, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageRequirements), findings, func() []ValidationFinding {
619: 			data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StageRequirements)
620: 			if readErr != nil {
621: 				return []ValidationFinding{finding("requirements.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageRequirements), "missing requirements", readErr.Error(), "Generate requirements.md.")}
622: 			}
623: 			return ValidateRequirementsContent(data)
624: 		})
625: 		if err != nil {
626: 			stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
627: 			_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
628: 			return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
629: 		}
630: 	}
631: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
632: 		err := fmt.Errorf("generated requirements.md failed validation")
633: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
634: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))
635: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages, Findings: findings}, err
636: 	}
637: 	stages := flowRequirementsSuccessStages(sp, now)
638: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now)); err != nil {
639: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages}, err
640: 	}
641: 	_ = s.cleanupPlanningStageSessions(ctx, sp, StageRequirements, runtimeResult)
642: 	return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, Runtime: runtimeResult, Stages: stages, Message: "requirements complete"}, nil
643: }

666: 		}

676: 	}

678: 		return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: req.To, DryRun: true, Message: prompt.Prompt}, nil
679: 	}
680: 	if s.runtime == nil {
681: 		err := fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for sprint-index flow")
682: 		stages := flowFailedStages(sp, req.To, err, now)
683: 		_ = SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, NewFlowState(sp, stages, now))

Now let me look at the domain types (FlowState, StageState, etc.), the reconcileExpiredAttempts function, and the tests for locks and verification locks. Also let me check `atomicWriteFile` in store_fs.go.

Key hypotheses to investigate:

1. **PID reuse / stale lock takeover race** in `acquireVerificationFileLock`: Two processes A and B. Lock exists owned by dead PID P1. Both read it, both see dead PID, both attempt `os.Remove(path)`. Process A removes successfully, then creates lock with its own PID. Process B's remove fails with ENOENT (ignored), then B tries O_EXCL create — this will fail because A holds it now... wait no: B's remove failed with ErrNotExist which is ignored, then loop continues to next attempt; B attempts OpenFile O_EXCL — fails since A recreated. Second iteration: reads lock file (A's), sees A alive → conflict. OK that's fine.

   But there's a subtler race: A removes stale lock, then before A creates new lock, B removes... B's remove gets ENOENT ignored... then both A and B attempt O_EXCL create. Only one wins. The other goes around loop again and sees winner alive. Fine.

   What about TOCTOU between reading the lock info and removing it? Process A reads lock (dead pid 100). Meanwhile, a *different* process C (pid 100 reused? or original owner restarted?) ... Actually consider: the lock is held by live process P. But P is not ultraplan — any process on the system with matching PID makes the lock appear live. Conversely, if the lock file was created by attacker with PID of some long-lived unrelated system process (e.g., PID 1 or a daemon), then verificationProcessAlive returns true forever → permanent DoS of mutation. That's an attacker-controlled input scenario: anyone who can write `.ultraplan/locks/sprint/*.lock` can pin the lock by writing `{"pid":1,...}`. But who can write those files? Someone with filesystem write access already owns the workspace; the threat model here is likely local files trusted. Hmm — flow-state.json itself is written into the repo, so a malicious contributor could commit a lock file? The lock dir is `.ultraplan/locks` inside the workspace root — plausibly committed to git! If `.ultrapran/` is checked into the repo (the planning workspace IS a git repo per frozen workspace commit), then a malicious collaborator could commit a lock file with PID 1 and project/sprint fields valid, causing permanent ErrVerificationConflict for everyone cloning it. Is that plausible? Let me check whether .ultraplan is gitignored. Let me look at the workspace repo.

   Also note: readVerificationFileLock validates Project/Sprint non-empty but doesn't check they match sprint.Project/sprint.Slug. Not necessarily a defect.

2. **`release()` ownership check compares AcquiredAt with Equal** — time equality after JSON round-trip: time.Time unmarshals RFC3339 with nanoseconds preserved, so Equal works if marshaled precisely. Marshal writes RFC3339Nano; unmarshal parses back exactly. OK.

3. **In-process mutex map keyed by sp.Path but `mutations` sync.Map shared across copies**: Service is a value type with pointer `mutations`. LoadOrStore then Delete — but nested acquireMutationContext reuses ctx marker so composite workflows don't deadlock. But what about two different Service instances in same process (e.g., server creates service per request)? Each NewService has its own mutations map → in-process layer doesn't protect across instances; only the O_EXCL file lock does. That's fine since file lock covers cross-instance.

4. **`ReconcileInterruptedMutation` swallows ErrVerificationConflict returning false,nil** — fine.

5. **Status() writes flow state without holding mutation lease**: Status calls SaveFlowState at line 292 without acquiring the mutation lock. This is "status-refresh write gating" mentioned in assignment: statusWrites flag gates whether Status writes. The concern from context pack unknowns: "Status-vs-writer race posture". Status computes refreshed stages from artifacts and saves; concurrent writer under lease saves too → lost update: e.g., during execute, Status refresh may write stage statuses derived from artifacts while execute updates task states... Actually flow state vs execute run state are separate. But review/smoke/QA records: Status preserves Review/Smoke/QA from loaded prior state. Race: Status loads state at T0, writer mutates review record at T1 (e.g., review completes, sets LastComplete), Status saves at T2 with old Review → loses completed evidence. SaveFlowState's backfill only applies when state.Review==nil; here Status sets refreshed.Review = state.Review (non-nil stale copy) → overwrites. So a plain `status` command racing a running verify/review could erase completion evidence → gate would then force re-verification (fail-safe direction?) or worse, mark stale=false with old evidence? Losing evidence means gate requires redo — reliability issue, availability not integrity. Severity moderate; concurrency window small. But is Status expected to be used while a mutation runs? The CLI presumably prevents concurrent ops via lease for mutations, but status is read-only-ish yet performs writes when statusWrites enabled. The design comment says WithoutStatusWrites is for "strictly read-only presentation surfaces" — implying default Status DOES write and races are accepted? Need to check callers: who uses NewService().Status vs WithoutStatusWrites. Let me grep.

6. **SaveFlowState DB-first routing + checkpoint duplication**: In DB-authoritative mode, save writes DB and ALSO file checkpoint when terminal. Then Load prefers DB. Checkpoint file is for portability. OK.

7. **loadFlowStateDatabase ignores DisallowUnknownFields / trailing checks / schema version validation at header level** — but ValidateFlowState is called afterwards in LoadFlowState (line 28). ValidateFlowState checks SchemaVersion == FlowStateSchemaVersion (v2). So DB legacy v1 records rejected. Good. But wait — json.Unmarshal(record.Header, &state) without DisallowUnknownFields: unknown fields tolerated in DB branch, unlike file branch. Minor inconsistency; validation still enforces core grammar. Not a strong finding.

Validation then passes. Read-time-only upgrade: never persisted unless something saves. Status saves though! Status → SaveFlowState(refreshed) persists migrated state even when nothing else changed. That's intended ("status refresh").

10. **interpretPreCodeContextStages sets inserted.LastRunAt only in skipped case; StatusReady case leaves LastRunAt zero** — cosmetic.

11. **ValidateFlowState stage path check**: `strings.HasPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(...)), "../")` plus resolveSprintContained. Note cleanRel == "." case handled in resolveSprintContained. Paths like "projects/x/sprints/y/../../.." ? Clean resolves to escape → caught. 12. **verificationProcessAlive EPERM treated as alive**: On systems with hidepid or different-user processes, kill(pid,0) gives EPERM meaning process exists but we can't signal — correct to treat as alive. But also: PID namespace differences — if lock created inside container with different PID mapping, stale detection breaks. Edge.

13. **The stale-lock removal race with two contenders where one removes the OTHER's fresh lock**: Scenario: Owner P1 acquires lock (writes file). Contender A opens... wait, O_EXCL fails, reads info, P1 alive → conflict return. No removal of live locks. Removal only after verifying PID dead. TOCTOU: P1 dies right after A reads? Then A removes lock — fine, P1 dead. Reverse: A reads lock showing dead PID X. Between read and Remove, PID X... irrelevant. BUT what if lock file is replaced between read and remove: A reads stale info (pid X dead); meanwhile legitimate new owner B (another contender) removed and recreated lock with live PID Y. A then os.Remove(path) — deletes B's LIVE lock! Then A creates its own lock. Now two processes hold "the lock": B thinks it owns (its release() will detect ownership changed and refuse release — good), but B continues working believing it holds the lease while A also proceeds → mutual exclusion broken. Window: between readVerificationFileLock and os.Remove in acquireVerificationFileLock lines 49–58. This is a genuine TOCTOU race in the layered lease. Probability low (requires three processes: dead-owner lock present, two contenders simultaneously). Observable bad outcome: two concurrent mutations corrupting flow-state (lost updates, torn multi-file transitions). The ownership-checked release mitigates release-side damage but not the mutual-exclusion break during operation. Is there mitigation elsewhere? The in-process sync.Map only guards same Service instance's mutations map... Different OS processes → nothing. So yes, real race. Severity: medium-low given narrow window, but it's the exact class the surface claims to guarantee ("O_EXCL pidfile with liveness"). Confidence high that code has the race; medium that it triggers in practice.

If reconcile found nothing to change but marker exists, they refuse to consume and error out. Per doctrine "cleanup-uncertain consumption rules" — deliberate: consuming requires actual reconciliation work. Hmm, but then how does the marker ever get consumed if there was genuinely nothing interrupted? First run with changes consumes. If no changes ever needed (spurious marker), permanent error loop. 21. **Lock file written AFTER O_EXCL create but content written non-atomically**: Between create and full write, another process could read empty/partial file → json.Unmarshal error → "unreadable lock" → ErrVerificationConflict returned to contender (fail closed). Actually wait — worse: contender reads partial file where PID parse succeeded? Partial write can't produce valid JSON with valid pid unless truncated at end — truncation yields invalid JSON. Safe.

Dead-owner recovery relies on readable PID; unreadable lock → hard error, manual intervention. Crash window tiny (create→write). But crash during write (power loss) leaves truncated file permanently blocking all mutations for that sprint until human deletes file. Reliability finding (low severity, real). If DB deleted/corrupted, fallback file is ancient → silent regression to old stage statuses? LoadFlowState falls back to file when DB record absent. Stale checkpoint misleads gates? Confirmed: 1. CLI `sprint

status` (sprint_commands.go:88,95) uses `sprint.NewService(...)` with statusWrites=true → Status WRITES flow-state.json on every CLI status invocation. 2. TUI: writable useCases (tui_commands.go:41-46 no readOnly). While an operation runs (`m.model.Running`), runViewTickMsg fires every second → refreshCmd → Dashboard → SprintSummaries → writable `service.Status()` per sprint — concurrent goroutine with the running operation (which holds the mutation lease and writes flow-state via review/smoke/verify/QA/execute writers). tea.Cmd runs in separate goroutines; bubbletea model updates serialize message handling but commands execute concurrently. Dashboard() is a blocking call in a Cmd goroutine while operation goroutine writes state. Race confirmed structurally. 3. Also two terminals: TUI open (polling) + CLI verification command in another terminal → cross-process race: TUI's Status write vs lease-holding CLI writer. The file lock does NOT exclude Status because Status never takes it. So Finding 1 (primary): Status flow-state write bypasses the mutation lease → lost-update can revert/clobber verification attempt records and completed evidence during long operations. Observable bad outcome: e.g., user runs `ultraplan sprint p s verify` in one terminal, keeps TUI/another `sprint status` running; when review completes and records LastComplete evidence + ActiveAttempt cleared, a concurrent Status save reverts Review to pre-completion snapshot (ActiveAttempt running / stale attempt), so the gate then reports review incomplete/expired-attempt; reconcileExpiredAttempts later marks the LIVE... wait actually after completion the owner process may have exited; reverted ActiveAttempt has OwnerPID of now-dead process → next ReconcileInterruptedMutation marks it timed_out → forces full re-review. Evidence erased → forced redo (availability), plus confusing incorrect audit trail. Could it ever UNDO a failure into a pass? Status recomputes Stale flags from current artifacts each time; preserved record fields like Verdict could survive from older snapshot? Scenario: review completes FAIL at T2 (writer saves verdict=fail). Status loaded at T1 (verdict=pass from previous cycle) saves at T3 → reverts fail→pass! Then gate sees pass?? But freshness: Status recomputes refreshed.Review.Stale using PrepareReview fingerprint comparison & artifact digest check (lines 269-279): stale=true if digest mismatch etc. After a new failing review run rewrote review.md, the OLD pass record's ArtifactDigest won't match new content hash → Stale=true → gate fails closed. Unless writer didn't change artifact digest... For smoke: fingerprintMismatch checks. QA summary: pointer validated. So integrity holds via digests; damage is availability/audit. Good — severity medium-high reliability, not a security bypass. Actually wait, there's one more subtle integrity angle: Status's SaveFlowState backfill — refreshed.Review non-nil always (copied), so no backfill issue. And what about racing ExecuteRunState? Status doesn't write run-state. Fine. Finding 1 confidence high. It's exactly the "Status-vs-writer race posture" unknown in context pack; my job was to resolve it — resolved as REAL defect (write path lacks synchronization). Hmm wait — let me double-check that SaveFlowState in Status isn't protected by some flock inside saveFlowStateWithHooks — no, plain temp+rename. And os.Rename atomic replace means readers see whole file (no torn read) — the issue is purely lost-update ordering. Also note: even without any mutation running, TWO concurrent Status invocations race harmlessly (same derived content). One more check for Finding 1 completeness: does `Status` skip save when state unchanged? No diff check — every poll rewrites. That also spams mtime → anything keying on UpdatedAt/mtime? freshness_policy uses fingerprints/digests not mtimes presumably. OK. Now Finding 2 (TOCTOU stale-lock takeover deleting live lock). Let me re-verify code path lines: acquireVerificationFileLock lines 49-58: ```go existing, readErr := readVerificationFileLock(path) ... if verificationProcessAlive(existing.PID) { return conflict } if removeErr := os.Remove(path); removeErr != nil && !errors.Is(removeErr, fs.ErrNotExist) { ... } ``` Then loop attempt++ → OpenFile O_EXCL again. Interleaving C1/C2 as described yields both holding. Note ALSO simpler variant: C2's Remove succeeds removing C1's NEW lock; C2 creates its own. C1 continues operating (it only detects ownership change at release()). So mutual exclusion broken for entire window. Real. Trigger requires: stale lock present (previous crash) AND ≥2 processes attempting acquisition near-simultaneously (retry loops, queued ops after server restart, cron). Plausible operationally after crashes — precisely when reconcile/storms happen. Severity medium (integrity of serialized mutations), likelihood low-medium. Report. Mitigating controls to acknowledge: release() ownership check prevents wrongful release; O_EXCL ensures single creator per removal; conflict errors are fail-closed. The residual hole is the unlink-not-CAS. Fix suggestion: stat inode before/after read and use unix.Unlinkat with dirfd+compare, or take parent-dir flock briefly during takeover, or rename stale file to unique name then recreate (rename is atomic; loser's rename fails ENOENT if winner already renamed). Actually simplest: `os.Rename(path, path+".stale.")` — only ONE contender's rename succeeds (atomic); others get ENOENT; then create O_EXCL; remove the renamed side file. Rename over existing name would clobber... rename(stale→uniqueName) moves it; second contender's rename fails since source gone. That's CAS-like. Good regression test possible with injected hooks? Hard to test race deterministically; test could simulate by monkeypatching? At minimum document. Finding 3 candidate: unreadable lock permanent wedge. Crash between O_EXCL create and Write leaves empty file → all future acquirers hit readVerificationFileLock error → ErrVerificationConflict forever until manual rm. Window is small (create→marshal→write→close, microseconds-ms) but crash/power-loss there permanently disables ALL mutations for that sprint (review/smoke/verify/qa/execute/reconcile all acquire lease!). ReconcileInterruptedMutation also acquires → recovery itself blocked. That's a real operability defect: self-healing exists for dead-but-readable owners, not for unreadable files. Severity low-medium reliability, confidence high mechanism (no self-heal path exists — verified: error returns immediately line 50-52). Counter-evidence: maybe some admin CLI removes locks? grep "locks/sprint" elsewhere. Also related: lock JSON valid but Project/Sprint empty → invalid identity error → same wedge. Attacker-controlled: anyone able to write workspace files can wedge all mutations by planting garbage lock (or pin live PID like 1). But such attacker already owns the workspace files (could delete everything) — not a trust boundary crossing. Skip security framing; keep reliability framing. Finding 4 candidate: cleanup-uncertain sticky wedge after partial reconcile failure (described earlier). Sequence: marker exists; reconcile changes execute tasks; SaveExecuteRunState ok; QA interrupted branch errors (e.g., qa state corrupt) → return err BEFORE marker consumption. Retry: nothing left changed → hasUncertainty && !changed → ErrCleanupUncertain forever. Manual intervention needed; marker file documents reason though. Fail-closed by design? The doctrine says cleanup-uncertain consumption is deliberate. The sticky case requires partial failure — operator sees explicit error naming the marker path. I'd rank low/informational; probably defensible design (fail-closed). Maybe include as minor with clear reasoning or list under defended/non-issues. Hmm. Actually wait, worse variant WITHOUT partial failure: marker exists, reconcile finds running tasks → marks failed → changed → consumes marker. Fine. Marker exists, NOTHING running (spurious marker after shutdown between operation end and marker write?) → RecordCleanupUncertain is called at server_shutdown deadline exhaustion DURING an operation presumably; if the operation actually finished its terminal writes before shutdown but cleanup (session cleanup?) was cut... then reconcile finds nothing to change → permanent error loop. Is that plausible? RecordCleanupUncertain called when ctx deadline exceeded during RunOperation cleanup phase. If flow-state terminal writes completed, reconcile changes nothing → stuck. Operator must rm .cleanup-uncertain.json manually. Documented? Check TRD §18.5 contract. Let me peek at workspace docs quickly for cleanup-uncertain contract to see whether manual deletion is prescribed remedy. Finding 5 candidate: migrateFlowStateV1 swallows hashFile error → "legacy-unverifiable" digest stored as ArtifactDigest. Then Status freshness check compares hashBytes(content) != ArtifactDigest → mismatch → Stale=true → forces re-review. Fail-safe. Fine. Finding 6: LoadFlowState v1 migration mutates nothing on disk (read-time-only) — BUT SaveFlowState backfill calls LoadFlowState which migrates in memory then saves v2 — meaning ANY subsequent save persists migration. With WithoutStatusWrites for read-only surfaces. By design. Finding 11: **saveFlowStateDatabase ignores s.now / clock** — tests only. Skip. Finding 12: **acquireMutation releases fileLock with `_ = fileLock.release()` ignoring error** — if ownership changed (shouldn't happen for legit owner), silently ignores; sync.Map entry deleted regardless. Crash of process whose PID got reused before removal... normal: owner dies → PID freed → reused by editor → lock looks ALIVE → blocked until editor closes (could be days). metadata.output:
### 18.5 Flow State

`flow-state.json` must be versioned and stored in the sprint root.

Required fields:

- schema version
- project name
- sprint slug
- updated timestamp
- per-stage status
- per-stage artifact path
- per-stage last run timestamp
- per-stage error, if any

Allowed statuses:

- missing
- ready
- complete
- failed
- skipped

Requirements:

- Writes must be atomic.
- Loading must reject malformed JSON and unsupported schema versions with clear diagnostics.
- Existing artifacts must be inspected to initialize or refresh flow state.
- `area-reasoning` is skipped only when `sprint-index.md` selects no reasoning templates.
- Execute may appear in Phase 2 flow state only after valid prerequisites through `plan`.
- No smoke, review, or issue stages may appear in Phase 2 flow state.
- Phase 3 flow state adds `review` after `execute` and `smoke` after `review`.
- Review and smoke stage state must distinguish execution status from verdict so a successfully completed investigation may truthfully report a failing verdict.
- Review and smoke state must record the governed input fingerprint used by the current artifact. A fingerprint mismatch makes the artifact stale.

### 18.5.1 Execute Run State

`.run-state.json` must be versioned and stored in the sprint root when execute begins.

Required fields:

- schema version
- project name
- sprint slug
- target repository path or workspace-relative target reference
- source `plan.md` path and content fingerprint where practical
- updated timestamp
- deterministic task records
- per-task status
- per-task attempts
- per-task timestamps
- per-task safe diagnostics
- per-task runtime metadata summaries where available

Allowed task statuses:

- pending
- running
- complete
- failed
- cancelled

Requirements:

- Writes must be atomic.
- Loading must reject malformed JSON and unsupported schema versions with clear diagnostics.
- Interrupted runs must be resumable without redoing complete tasks unless explicitly forced.
- Stale running tasks must be recovered to a retryable or failed state with a diagnostic.
- Task IDs must be stable for the same validated `plan.md`.
- Execute must not mutate Git state automatically.
- Execute must not run smoke, review, or issue workflows.
- Target repository writes must be constrained to the configured target implementation directory unless explicitly configured otherwise.

### 18.6 Stage Validators

Planning validators are product behavior owned by `internal/sprint`.

`requirements.md` validator checks:

- file exists
- no placeholders
- required sections exist: sprint goal, required outputs, acceptance criteria, non-goals

`sprint-index.md` validator checks:

- file exists
- required sections exist: sprint scope, selected contracts, selected evidence reports, selected reasoning templates, required review protocols
- all selected catalog paths are present in `project-index.md`

280:Phase 2 includes controlled implementation execution through `execute`. Phase 3 extends the same sprint module through `review` and `smoke`. It keeps only the current `review.md` and `smoke.md` in the sprint root; detailed smoke runs and issue evidence remain in the external harness. `sprint` must not model general-purpose issue tracking, automatic product fixes, or Git mutation as workflow stages.
349:Until Sprint 35 reasoning changes the ownership topology, the server owns every worker it starts. Graceful shutdown enters draining, rejects new mutations, cancels all server-owned workers through their canonical cancellation functions, waits for bounded cleanup/reconciliation, persists truthful terminal or uncertain outcomes, then closes SSE/HTTP. Browser disconnect is subscription loss only and never operation cancellation. Run identity and retained observation survive the server even when the worker does not.
360:track owner lease, heartbeat, fencing, and process/runtime identity
363:reconcile stale, interrupted, and cleanup-uncertain work conservatively
614:Do not reject current-sprint code only because it lacks a port or registrar. Reject it when a concrete dependency crosses a volatile boundary, hides side effects, makes tests require private mutation, or couples product modules in a way this document does not allow.
621:Stable public JSON/release: canonical structured error payloads, stable machine-readable error codes, scenario tests, documented compatibility, and migration/rejection behavior for durable formats.
703:- Writable investigators require isolated validated workspaces; isolation uncertainty blocks mutation.

### Content and retrieval boundary

An optional focused content-metadata package may eventually parse versioned frontmatter, stable IDs, semantic blocks, relationships, and revision-aware evidence while preserving legacy Markdown bodies. It must not become a universal product artifact service or persistence layer. Explicit project/sprint selections continue to govern agent context; retrieval may propose or display candidates but cannot silently alter governance.

Derived retrieval begins with deterministic semantic chunks and a measured lexical baseline. Embeddings, automatic prompt injection, and hosted indexing require separate evidence. Every record retains exact authoritative text, status, authority, provenance, source revision, and rebuild version.

### Verification and repair boundary

Keep Conformance Review, empirical QA, adjudication, and repair distinct:

- Conformance Review remains read-only and preserves `review`/`review.md` compatibility.
- QA maps changed behavior into bounded verification surfaces and owns theory/evidence gathering, not production repair.
- Writable investigators require isolated validated workspaces; isolation uncertainty blocks mutation.
- A global adjudicator grounds expectations, rejects invalid/flaky evidence, groups root causes, and alone promotes repairable issues.
- Repair consumes frozen issue packets, changes only allowed production scope, cannot weaken evidence or requirements, and is progressively reverified.
- Automatic repair has fixed cycle/reopen limits and explicit `blocked`, `escalated`, and `stalled` outcomes.

Detailed QA attempt state belongs outside `flow-state.json`; flow state keeps canonical summaries, freshness, verdicts, and pointers.

### Persistence boundary

Operational run durability in Sprint 35 does not decide the later authority of authored product artifacts. The run store may use the smallest mechanism that proves concurrent acceptance, ordered append, liveness, replay, bounded retention, and recovery, while Markdown and package-owned workflow artifacts retain their existing authority.

Do not inject a generic virtual filesystem. If concrete browser workflows prove the need for alternate product-artifact persistence, define focused interfaces in the consuming product modules—for example `project.Repository`, `sprint.Repository`, and `study.Repository`. Repository contracts express semantic atomic stage commits, immutable artifact revisions, and optimistic concurrency, not paths, SQL, or transaction handles.

Filesystem and any later SQLite adapters must pass shared contract suites. Persistence selection occurs once at composition, one authority is active at a time, and migration/import/export is explicit. Source repositories, Git operations, code search, builds/tests, and agent execution workspaces remain real filesystems. No silent dual writes or synchronization precede an explicit authority decision.

### Knowledge graph boundary

A future graph starts, if justified, as a deterministic in-memory read-only projection over explicit artifact IDs and relationships. Every material edge carries provenance, origin (`explicit`, `structural`, `deterministic`, or visibly weaker `inferred`), status, and revision. Inferred edges cannot satisfy governance, completion, implementation, or verification. Persistent graph storage remains a disposable index and a dedicated graph database is not assumed.

### Stop/go rule

Each boundary is earned by the next demonstrated use case. Stop when metadata becomes unreliable bureaucracy, QA isolation/evidence is uncertain, repair does not converge, lexical search answers the real corpus, SQLite lacks concrete product value, or graph traversal does not outperform direct evidence inspection.

## Final Principle

```text
Platform owns generic capabilities.
Modules own product behavior.
Logic stays near the state it transforms.
Interfaces appear only at external or volatile boundaries.
```

It may depend on `app` use-case interfaces and plain result types. It must not import `study`, `project`, `sprint`, runtime adapters, or process adapters directly. It must not own workflow state machines, validators, prompts, runtime execution, smoke invocation, verdicts, product locks, durable run identity, or durable recovery.

The server operation hub is transport-lifecycle state, not product state. It may retain bounded delivery buffers and subscribers, but it cannot be the authoritative run registry or sole event history. Slow or disconnected SSE subscribers must never block an app operation. A server restart or browser-session change replaces delivery state without erasing the durable run.

Until Sprint 35 reasoning changes the ownership topology, the server owns every worker it starts. Graceful shutdown enters draining, rejects new mutations, cancels all server-owned workers through their canonical cancellation functions, waits for bounded cleanup/reconciliation, persists truthful terminal or uncertain outcomes, then closes SSE/HTTP. Browser disconnect is subscription loss only and never operation cancellation. Run identity and retained observation survive the server even when the worker does not.

### Durable execution control boundary

Sprint 35 introduces a product-owned operational boundary shared by CLI, TUI, and web. Its semantic responsibilities are fixed even though its concrete package, coordinator topology, and store are reasoning decisions:

```text
accept run durably before starting work
assign stable run / attempt / stage / task correlations
publish one workspace-wide lifecycle projection
record sanitized monotonically ordered events before fan-out
track owner lease, heartbeat, fencing, and process/runtime identity
route authorized idempotent cancellation to the current owner
arbitrate exactly one terminal outcome
reconcile stale, interrupted, and cleanup-uncertain work conservatively
apply bounded retention with explicit cursor gaps and tombstones
```

Product modules still decide whether their own stages and artifacts succeeded. The shared boundary records and projects execution facts; it does not replace sprint flow state, study run state, execute task state, Markdown artifacts, Git/source state, or external smoke evidence.

The final design must reason explicitly about a dedicated product module versus package-owned repositories coordinated through `app`; filesystem journal versus SQLite or another local store; one coordinator versus fenced multi-process writers; worker cancellation versus adoption after owner loss; and same-host versus shared-filesystem multi-host guarantees. Whichever choices are selected must satisfy the same public lifecycle, replay, security, migration, and fault-injection contracts.

The first web UI is server-rendered and progressively enhanced. A frontend framework or JavaScript build pipeline is not part of the Phase 4 foundation; add one only after real client-side complexity earns it.
